title: Beginner React JS
description: This is a competency-based course designed for the indentured website developer apprentice.  This course provides project-based assignments on the use of the front end library React JS to build advanced websites.
learning_objectives: Break an interface into a tree of reusable components
Pass data through a component tree with props and composition
Manage component state and respond to user events
Render lists and conditional interfaces correctly
Load and display remote data from a component
Build interfaces that are accessible and responsive
Prototype a feature before committing to an implementation
Work from a project plan to deliver a feature increment
Present a working React application and the reasoning behind it
prerequisites: Comfortable with modern JavaScript: arrow functions, destructuring, array methods, and modules
Working knowledge of HTML and CSS

sequencing_rationale: The first seven lessons follow React's own dependency order - decomposition, then props, then state, then the rendering patterns state drives, then forms, then effects - because each is unusable without its predecessor and every one of them is a common place for a beginner to form a wrong model. Accessibility and responsiveness come after forms rather than at the end: forms are where the accessibility rules bite hardest, and leaving them to a final lesson teaches learners they are an afterthought. Prototyping and project planning sit late on purpose - they are judgment lessons, and a learner cannot judge between two implementations of a feature until they can build either one. The capstone closes with a demo because the pathway's presentation competency needs a real artifact. SCOPE ASSUMPTIONS: the intake description is short and complete but names only 'project-based assignments on the use of the front end library React JS', with 100 hours as the main evidence of depth - the largest course in the pathway. The outline assumes function components and hooks only (no class components), a single-page app with no router and no external state library (react200 owns both), and client-side data fetching against an existing API rather than one the learner writes. Assumed out of scope: TypeScript, testing libraries, server-side rendering, and build-tool configuration beyond a scaffolded starter.

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can build a user interface from reusable components that manage local and shared state.
proposed_competencies.rationale: This is the entire subject of the pathway's largest course, and the only tag available is D2-S1-C04, which says 'build program features using appropriate languages and development methods' without distinguishing component-based UI construction from any other kind of feature work.

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can meet WCAG-level accessibility requirements in a component-based interface, including keyboard operation and semantic markup.
proposed_competencies.rationale: D5-S1-C04 covers contributing to accessible and responsive designs and D6-S1-C01 covers monitoring for accessibility compliance, but lesson 08 assesses the learner building to a stated conformance level, which sits between the two and is named by neither.
